newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta harvest 50 pct complete, rain delays north.
newsitem.headline: Alberta harvest 50 pct complete, rain delays north.

text.p: Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete on good progress in the south but rain slowed activity at and north of Edmonton, Alberta Agriculture said in a crop report for the week ended Sunday.

Southern Alberta's harvest was more than half complete while weekend rains delayed harvest progress in the north. Overall, about 50 percent of Alberta's crops were in the bin, slightly behind last year.
Southern Alberta made good harvest progress with many districts 80 to 90 percent complete. Areas around Medicine Hat and Vulcan have 50 to 60 percent of their crops to combine.

Central Alberta's harvest advanced significantly with the eastern half about 50 percent complete and the west 40 percent done. Weekend rains prevented more progress and will delay harvest a few more days. Yields were seen average to above average.

Northeast Alberta combined 50 percent of its crops except in the northern region with five to 20 percent of the crop in the bin. Canola yields were seen below average. All other yields were seen at or above average.
Northwest Alberta's harvest varied from 10 to 25 to 40 percent complete with significant rain delays.
Peace River Valley's farmers swathed 30 to 40 percent of their crops and less than 10 percent was combined because of excess moisture.
